title: The conveyor, designed
done: Read snapall's and lab-agent's delivery workflows (release, verify, publish - about 500 nearly identical lines each); designed one conveyor that projects call at a pinned version with one declaration; recorded the decisions and the path.
considered: One signing key for the whole commons; deb and rpm repositories first.
rejected: Both, for now - see the decisions.

title: The conveyor's first delivery
done: Wrote the two reusable workflows, checked by actionlint; moved lab-agent onto them (187 lines became a declaration, four copied helpers removed); its release v0.1.47 was the conveyor's first delivery - binaries, provenance, PKGBUILD, signed repository, real install, all green. Published as v1.0.0 and the moving v1.
rejected: Not needed: a pending release made the first run a real one, which tests more.

title: The packaging container has the makedepends too
done: The first real second package (sxmo-utils, lab-tools) failed in the signing container: its APKBUILD compiled in package() (make install), where only alpine-sdk was installed, so setcap and the headers were missing. The signing container now runs abuild deps (apk installs of the APKBUILD makedepends) before the key is written, and a fixture package needs setcap in package() so the test fails without it. The APKBUILD was also given a build() (lab-tools PR 169) so the compile runs in the build container, which never has the key.
considered: Installing the makedepends after the key; a build() check in the conveyor.
rejected: After the key: the key would sit beside apk install scripts; a check: a project may legitimately compile in package().

title: alpine.yml holds several packages in one repository
done: Looked at who calls alpine.yml (only linux-phone-oco/lab-tools, found by reading every workflow of the conveyor, lens, linux-phone-oco, grenudi, creation-guidelines and open-commons-observatory repositories) and at the org (conveyor and lens: no other apk tooling; alpine.yml is what built and signed lpoco-health). Wrote the test first (tests/alpine/run.sh, failing on v1: abuild cannot checksum a source beside the APKBUILD), then copied the APKBUILD folder whole, kept the live repository's other packages in the signed index, derived the front page and the verify step from the index, and stopped a deploy that would lose a live package. v1.2.0.
considered: The merge in the publish job.
rejected: Needs the key outside its container - see the decision.

title: The apk page names each package's licence, origin and source
done: Read lab-tools #211 (license=, url=, "# Origin:" in each APKBUILD, check-apk-origin.sh), the live page (no licence, origin or source) and the page step. Wrote the test first (tests/alpine/run.sh: the page must give each fixture package its licence from the index, its Origin line, its source and the folder at the release tag, keep the first package's through the second's run, expand a source at a public tag from pkgver, and cope with a live package that has no record); it failed at the first release: no section for fixt-one. Then the publish job's page step: origins/NAME.json written from the APKBUILD sourced in a read-only container, the others fetched from the live pages, one section per package.
considered: The index alone: it carries L: and U:, not the origin or the source.
